headline: Revenue climbs on launches while losses widen
summary_short: Revenue of $191.2M rose 57.4% y/y (down 2.4% q/q) on continued AUVELITY and SUNOSI growth; GAAP net loss widened to $64.5M ($1.26/share) on higher R&D and SG&A tied to the Alzheimer's launch and a one-time acquisition charge.
summary_long: Revenue rose 57.4% y/y to $191.2M (down 2.4% q/q), led by AUVELITY's 59% y/y growth to $153.2M following April's FDA approval for Alzheimer's-related agitation, plus SUNOSI's 34% y/y growth. Gross margin held near 92%. R&D rose to $52.7M on a one-time acquisition-related charge tied to the balipodect (AXS-20) deal; SG&A rose to $185.0M on AUVELITY DTC advertising and SYMBRAVO commercialization. GAAP net loss widened to $64.5M ($1.26/share) from $59.4M a year ago. The release gives no numeric financial guidance, only a qualitative statement that cash is sufficient to reach cash-flow positivity. Cash fell to $305.1M from $322.9M last quarter.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by AUVELITY's 59% y/y revenue growth to $153.2M and SUNOSI's 34% y/y growth to $33.9M; SYMBRAVO added $4.1M in its early launch.
Loss widened as R&D rose to $52.7M on a one-time acquisition-related expense and SG&A rose to $185.0M on AUVELITY DTC advertising and SYMBRAVO commercialization spend.
Net loss widened to $64.5M, which the release attributes to the same R&D and SG&A increases; it also discloses $23.4M of stock-based compensation within the loss.
A wider net loss combined with a modestly higher weighted diluted share count (51.2M vs 48.9M y/y) deepened the per-share loss.
Cash fell q/q as operating losses and pre-launch/commercial spend outpaced inflows; not separately reconciled to a single cause in the release.
CEO cited a "tremendous start to 2026": AUVELITY's FDA approval for Alzheimer's-related agitation, a full launch on track for June 2026, and the added balipodect (AXS-20) pipeline asset.
